source.title: [Replication] Conjecture's Sparse Coding in Toy Models

record.file_problem: The post text is present, but the embedded comparison figures are missing; only their captions are available, so their results cannot be read.
record.tranche_reason: It reports a replication of toy-model sparse-coding experiments and lists measures relevant to superposition, but the available text does not provide their results.
record.gate_note: The post names comparisons of mean maximum cosine similarity with true features and dead-neuron counts, but gives no values or explicit outcomes. The captions alone do not support result rows.
record.test_reason: The post replicates a sparse-autoencoder method on synthetic data in which features are put into superposition by construction. It reports only how well the dictionary recovers those planted features: mean maximum cosine similarity (MMCS) and dead-neuron counts. It never measures how often or how strongly real or toy-model neurons are polysemantic, or why. So it relies on superposition as a premise and evaluates its own decomposition tool. It does not test any version, including V3: recovering planted features does not show that neurons in trained networks are polysemantic because of superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say they replicated the toy-model section of Sharkey et al.'s sparse-coding post and released code. They state no numerical results in text; the comparisons are figures only, absent here. They plan to extend the work to small transformers and to automated interpretability.
record.recipe_differences: The post describes a sparse-coding toy-model replication of another post, rather than the methods of the cited original sources; procedural details and outcomes are not present in the available text.
record.problems: The comparison figures and their values are unavailable in the supplied text; no controls, uncertainty estimates, or performance results are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows could be extracted: the post supplies captions for MMCS and dead-neuron comparisons but no accessible values or explicit result statements.

untested.parts: All: no vision-model neurons are examined.
All: no language-model MLP neurons are examined. Small transformers are listed only as future work.
All: superposition is built into the synthetic data, not inferred from trained neurons.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests' and tranche T2 are corrected to uses_without_test and T4. V3 is not tested: the post evaluates a mitigation and decomposition tool, the sparse autoencoder, on data with planted superposition. The MMCS and dead-neuron figures are unavailable, but even if readable they would measure the tool's performance, not neuron polysemanticity. No rows were extracted, and none are needed.
